text:
leo: Quick follow-up from RFC: instead of ad-hoc inline checks, propose a small AuthZ/Policy Facade that centralizes tenant policy, quota windows, and model access lists. Goal: accelerate policy changes and make audits straightforward.

anya: Strong +1 on auditability. Two immediate constraints i see: (1) hotpath latency (generation p50 target < 18ms) and (2) policy datastore scale for >10k tenants.

devon: For latency we can adopt a two-tier approach: local per-worker LRU cache + async refresh, with the facade returning `policy_version` and `lease_ms`. Worker uses lease to avoid thundering herds.

leo: Thinking `lease_ms` default 250ms for token validity and 2000ms for route-level quotas. Workers can override via config per deployment class.

sam: On datastore scale: we should shard policy store by tenant-hash and allow colocated read replicas. Facade will only serve policy read paths and push updates to replicas via changefeed. Writes (policy changes) go through control-plane service and update head.

anya: We also need deterministic quota accounting. Shadow runs will be tricky since we can't double-count. During shadow mode, facade should include `shadow_token` in response and not increment real counters. After cutover, a replay job will reconcile shadowed events into authoritative counters with idempotency keys.

devon: Agree on replay. Add a `replay_key` returned in shadow mode. Runtime should log requests with `replay_key` and `req_id`. We'll use that for a one-shot reconcile run.

ops-bot: Add alert: `authz.facade.latency_p95 > 50ms` and `policy.replay.failure_rate > 0.1%`. Also trace span `authz.check.local_cache_hit`.

leo: Private deployment constraints: packaged helm chart + sidecar-only mode optional. Sidecar-only mode will expose `CheckLocal()` via unix-socket to avoid RPC hop. That mode requires local policy sync agent and may be recommended for high-QPS, low-latency installs.

sam: Security: facade should accept signed control-plane JWTs for policy writes; runtime calls use short-lived mTLS tokens. For private installs, support HSM-backed signing.

anya: Migration plan suggestion: 1) implement facade read-only endpoint and proto; 2) enable shadow calls (non-enforcing) from runtime with `X-Shadow-Mode: true`; 3) run shadow for 7d collecting diffs; 4) run replay to sanity-check accounting; 5) switch to enforcement in 1-2 regions; 6) global roll.

devon: For performance spike validation, i'll run sims with 3 miss-rate profiles: 0.5%, 5%, 20% and measure end-to-end p50/p95. Will add a config knob to change local cache TTL dynamically.

leo: Ownership: eng-runtime implements client cache + replay logging; eng-platform owns policy datastore and reconciliation jobs; infra owns helm packaging and sidecar image; ops owns runbooks and SLOs.

sam: Protos: keep them tiny: `Check(req) => {allow, policy_version, lease_ms, shadow_key?}`. No model lists inline; instead return `policy_ref` and worker can fetch model list blob if needed (cached).

anya: One more ops note: when facade responds with `allow=false` include `deny_code` (rate_limit|blocked_model|tenant_suspended) to simplify client metrics and incident analysis.

infra-bot: FYI: will add packaging ticket and chart template skeleton.

leo: ok i'll draft short RFC with proto sketch, rollout checklist, and perf spike assignment to devon. tl;dr: centralize policy for agility and auditability; mitigate latency risk with local cache, lease, sidecar mode, and staged rollouts.

devon: I'll post bench numbers (p50/p95) and trace samples by EOW.

ops-bot: Reminder: include `authz.facade` in service map and add heartbeat metric.
